newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Egis Q1 profit, export in line with.
newsitem.headline: Egis Q1 profit, export in line with.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt said on Wednesday that its domestic sales were below target, while its exports and profits were in line with budget in the first quarter of 1997.

Egis, 50.91 percent by France's Servier S.A., released its earnings report this morning and said it posted after-tax profits of 1.796 billion forints as against 1.651 billion in the first three months of 1996.
The company's quarterly total sales rose to 6.899 billion forints from 6.126 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
"The company's domestic sales amounted to 3.498 billion forints, remaining 13 percent below the domestic turnover of the same period of last year," Egis said in its report.

"In the first quarter of 1996 wholesalers purchased substantial stocks of medicines in anticipation of price increases, while this did not characterise the market in the beginning of 1997," the company said.
"In addition, certain seasonal factors were not favourable for Egis's products either."
The company generated exports of $19.9 million in the first three months of the year, making a 35 percent rise in dollar terms over the same period of 1996.

"A rise in exports to the CIS countries of more than 50 percent in dollar terms, the launch of Egis's Tensiomin (blood pressure reducer) product in the U.K. and a favourable rise in bulk export contributed the most to the increase in exports," it said.
For 1997 the company expects a 20 percent increase in sales from 24.687 billion forints in 1996 and aims a rise of 16 percent in operating profits from 5.011 billion last year.
